॥ Om. The secondary meaning is not derived from the word “Self” (Atman). ॥ 1/1/6 ॥

It is also not appropriate to say, “The secondary Self is visible and speakable, and is without qualities.” This is because of the word “Self” (Atman). As stated in the Vamana Upanishad: “That which is devoid of all qualities, free from all defects, and free from the need for negation or affirmation is called the Self (Atman). That which is of a nature different from this is, according to the wise, the non-Self (Anatman). The word ‘Self’ is used in a secondary sense for the non-Self.” Also, as stated in the Talavakara Brahmana: “There are two forms of Brahman: the Self and the non-Self. Of these, the one that is the Self is eternal, pure, absolute, and without qualities. The one that is not of this nature is the non-Self.” Furthermore, the primary meaning does not apply to the secondary sense. ॥ 6 ॥
